t: From the city of Assur on the Tigris, Assyria grew from a merchant network into the largest empire the world had yet seen.
Its provinces, royal couriers, siege engineers and mass deportations became models for Babylon and Persia.
Overstretched and hated by its subjects, it was destroyed by Medes and Babylonians in barely sixty years after its peak.
dyk: The Library of Ashurbanipal at Nineveh preserved the standard version of the Epic of Gilgamesh, one of the oldest surviving works of literature.
ev: Assur emerges as an independent city-state after the fall of the Third Dynasty of Ur
Tukulti-Ninurta I conquers Babylon and captures its Kassite king
Adad-nirari II launches the Neo-Assyrian revival
Tiglath-pileser III takes the throne and reorganises army and provinces
Samaria falls and the population of the Kingdom of Israel is deported
Esarhaddon conquers Egypt, bringing the empire to its greatest extent
Babylonians and Medes destroy the Assyrian capital Nineveh
Ashur-uballit II fails to retake Harran and vanishes from the record
